script.base: Morning-of kickoff read for CAR@SF only, using the pack line SF -7.5 and total 48.5. Implied team totals are San Francisco 28.0 and Carolina 20.5, so the book expects the 49ers to lead and both teams to score. Base flow: San Francisco is in front by a score by halftime and leans on the run late. Christian McCaffrey has handled 53 carries for 217 yards over weeks 9-11 (about 17.7 carries and 72 rush yards a game) with Brian Robinson in a real complementary role (21 carries, 118 yards, 5.62 YPC). Carolina, getting 7.5, can stay on schedule early with Rico Dowdle (62 carries, 228 yards, 3.68 YPC last 3, plus 13 targets) but will throw more if the margin reaches two scores. Tetairoa McMillan is the vertical answer (26 targets, 236 yards, 268 air yards last 3). Dowdle is the checkdown (76 rec yards, -35 air yards). Pace from a 48.5 total is moderate, not a slog and not a 55-point shootout. No wind or rain number is saved, so the script does not lean weather.
script.flip1: San Francisco gets up big early at Levi's. CMC and Jauan Jennings late snaps stall the way a clock-kill lead stalls quarterback and WR yards, Robinson mops up carries, and Carolina abandons the run. Dowdle's rush line dies, Chuba Hubbard is even less involved than his 12 carries over three weeks, and McMillan plus Xavier Legette see garbage-time targets.
script.flip2: Carolina hangs around or leads. SF blitzes only 24 percent and Carolina's EPA per dropback is -0.20 versus the blitz but 0.00 with no blitz, so a clean Young game keeps it close. The 49ers then have to throw: Jennings (20 targets, 166 yards, 184 air last 3), George Kittle (19 targets, 183 yards, 119 air) and CMC receiving (22 targets, 173 yards). Robinson's carries get squeezed. Dowdle keeps a full rush share. Both defenses have bled the middle (SF 9.72 YPA on 75 throws, CAR 8.96 on 73), so the shootout flip is the other way 48.5 is light.

San Francisco's overlap is the run game plus Kittle and CMC short-intermediate work against Carolina's 4.59 YPC, Rozeboom and Wallace both out, and 8.96 middle YPA. Robinson at 5.62 YPC on 21 carries is the rush piece of that overlap. Jennings (184 air yards) is the 49ers' vertical piece, not the soft-middle piece. pre_mortem: It is Monday and the CAR@SF card lost. Robinson lost because Carolina led at Levi's and the 49ers never ran: McCaffrey took the few early carries, Robinson saw three or four rushes and finished in the teens, or a first-quarter fumble parked him. The 24-yard floor in the last four was still a positive-script game, and Carolina allowing 4.59 YPC does not matter if the carries are not there. Rozeboom and Wallace being out is irrelevant in a pass script. Hubbard lost because Dowdle exited after this morning report, Hubbard inherited a 10-to-12 carry share against a front missing Beal, and one of San Francisco's 23 runs of 10-plus this year was his, clearing 55.5 without a full season role. That counter is real. It is still weaker than a 62-to-12 carry split and four straight combined lines of 34 or less, so the leg stays flagged for the human rather than sized. Weather is the unknown that could also flip a rush lean, and no forecast was saved.
